svg.aria-label: Five human needs running through the field, drawn as Metro lines, with a station for each organization that reaches for a need. The table below lists every station and its evidence.
svg.text: Five Human Needs Running Through the Field

Under everything 50 organizations around The Labs do, and what three voices inside it told us, is a person who needs something. Each line is one of those needs, named for the research behind it. Each station is an organization reaching for it.
Dorst’s step 5, Themes. Field from desk research logged Nov 6; needs read Nov 9, 2026. Hover a station for its evidence; every station is in the table below.

circle.title: Alumni, C01–C03, Coherence: asked for a clearer roadmap from individual work into team pods
Alumni, C01–C03, Not Alone: “most valuable” was almost entirely the people
Alumni, C01–C03, Belonging: 7 of 11 still in touch with their team; one still building a venture from it
Organizers, Coherence: the biggest problem is cognitive load: knowing what’s next, and what’s expected
Organizers, Not Alone: organizer delays become participant emergencies
Organizers, Belonging: everyone sees The Labs through the Cycle; no before or after
The Problem Owner, Mattering: employers judge us against multi-million-dollar institutions
The Problem Owner, Coherence: how it all fits together isn’t written down anywhere
The Problem Owner, Not Alone: there is no one whose job it is to help people navigate
The Problem Owner, Belonging: leaving the Cycle means leaving The Labs
The Problem Owner, Believing I Can: people aren’t sure they’re allowed to go off on their own
DC Public Library, Mattering: will track engagement and completion to refine its cohort
DC Public Library, Coherence: classes tiered basic, intermediate, advanced; orientation before the Labs
DC Public Library, Not Alone: its 2025 AI cohort formed six pods
DC Public Library, Believing I Can: from “passive centers of learning” to “active destinations for creativity”
Arlington Public Library, Coherence: serves “beginning and advanced makers”: a route from one to the other
Arlington Public Library, Believing I Can: a card and an agreement, and you’re a maker
Montgomery County Libraries, Mattering: résumé clinics, LinkedIn reviews and headshots; counted by attendance
Montgomery County Libraries, Believing I Can: a 2025 focus on federal employees remaking their careers after the cuts
Fairfax County Library, Not Alone: Tech Tutors: one-to-one help
Prince George’s County Library, Mattering: librarians certified in the workforce board’s own credential
Prince George’s County Library, Not Alone: librarians trained to help residents find work
Public Library Association, Not Alone: AI knowledge for all library staff first, so they can help the public
Urban Libraries Council, Mattering: libraries as under-recognized workforce institutions; wants them named in law
Urban Libraries Council, Belonging: concedes most libraries lack dedicated funding for workforce programs
IMLS, Belonging: 2025: grants stopped and restarted; continuity, not outcomes, was the issue
DC Employment Services, Mattering: measures placements, certifications and employer engagement
DC Employment Services, Not Alone: a case-management pipeline of services
DC Workforce Investment Council, Mattering: aligns training with employer demand, counted in completions
Employ Prince George’s, Not Alone: counseling for about 500 federal workers, with about 50 paid slots
Employ Prince George’s, Belonging: replacing lost revenue; a job center may close
Employ Prince George’s, Believing I Can: converts résumés from federal format
Virginia Career Works Northern, Coherence: reemployment through career navigation
Virginia Career Works Northern, Not Alone: delivered by case managers
WorkSource Montgomery, Not Alone: a hub with counselors for federal workers
WorkSource Montgomery, Believing I Can: encourages specialized federal workers “to consider entrepreneurship”
US Department of Labor, Mattering: AI literacy through registered apprenticeships and skills standards
US Department of Labor, Coherence: pilots pathways into entry-level roles
Council of Governments, Talent Capital, Coherence: one platform of listings and AI agents for career navigation
Greater Washington Board of Trade, Mattering: credentials recognized across three jurisdictions
Greater Washington Board of Trade, Coherence: a resource guide for a system split across three jurisdictions
Greater Washington Board of Trade, Belonging: measure long-term outcomes, not “short-term placements”

svg.text: no theme in what we found

circle.title: Greater Washington Partnership, Mattering: an employer-recognized credential; the region as a global hub
NSF AI-Ready America, Coherence: state hubs must keep a public inventory of resources
America Achieves, Mattering: success is placement and wage data, validated by employers
America Achieves, Coherence: a vision that everyone has a clear path to a good job
Jobs for the Future, Coherence: state career-navigation platforms; AI material written too hard to read
National Skills Coalition, Mattering: worker voice; AI should strengthen working people, not sideline them
Burning Glass Institute, Mattering: workers are visible in its data only through postings and job changes
Burning Glass Institute, Coherence: the career ladder, losing its lower rungs
Opportunity@Work, Mattering: a labor market where “all talent can shine”; the degree screen is the barrier
Opportunity@Work, Believing I Can: only 15% of STARs call themselves a STAR
Anthropic Economic Futures, Coherence: evidence on what AI is doing to work, at the scale of the economy
Per Scholas, Mattering: publishes wage outcomes
Per Scholas, Belonging: an alumni Career Accelerator after the course
Per Scholas, National Capital Region, Mattering: employers are the customer
Per Scholas, National Capital Region, Not Alone: coaching for two years after
Per Scholas, National Capital Region, Belonging: two-year alumni support
Year Up United, Mattering: skills-first hiring; its own assessment limits who it can serve
Year Up United, Belonging: placement and alumni engagement
Year Up, National Capital Region, Coherence: lists its training as job postings, where job seekers already look
Merit America, Mattering: headline metric is cumulative wage gain
Merit America, Not Alone: the working adult needs a coach
Climb Hire, Not Alone: the missing ingredient is relationships; pods are the unit
Climb Hire, Belonging: the network is the route after the program
Urban Alliance, Mattering: measured by a randomized trial; to level the playing field
Urban Alliance, Not Alone: coaching through the last year of school
UDC Workforce Development, Mattering: documents and an assessment at the door
UDC Workforce Development, Coherence: a “No Wrong Door” policy; sector pathways
NOVA Workforce (NOVAnext), Mattering: a quick certification, paid by scholarship
NOVA Workforce (NOVAnext), Believing I Can: help federal workers “transition to new careers”
Byte Back (closed 2024), Belonging: results, but no sustained funding; closed after 27 years
Byte Back (closed 2024), Believing I Can: participants lacked confidence, not computers
OpenAI Academy, Mattering: 10 million Americans certified by 2030
Civic Tech DC, Not Alone: a recurring room, and a name that says what they do
Civic Tech DC, Belonging: kept meeting after its national hub withdrew in 2023
Alliance of Civic Technologists, Not Alone: a federation of peers
Alliance of Civic Technologists, Belonging: “brigades need to be able to be stable”
Code for America, Belonging: ended its volunteer network in 2023
Digital Inclusion Alliance, Not Alone: the digital navigator: a trusted person at the first threshold
Digital Inclusion Alliance, Belonging: its navigator funding was terminated in 2025
Greater Washington Community Foundation, Coherence: seeded Talent Capital and a regional data dashboard
Greater Washington Community Foundation, Belonging: nonprofit capacity and resilience
Meyer Foundation, Not Alone: community-centric power building
Meyer Foundation, Belonging: organizer sustainability

svg.text: no theme in what we found

circle.title: Clark Foundation (spent down), Belonging: spent down to zero in 2025 and left the field
Clark Foundation (spent down), Believing I Can: to help people reach their “full potential”
Ballmer Group, Mattering: economic mobility, measured
Ballmer Group, Belonging: large, flexible, multi-year grants
Gates Foundation, Mattering: credentials of value for millions more learners
Gates Foundation, Not Alone: AI to free advisors (some with 400+ students) for personal support
Google.org, Mattering: success counted in people trained
Lumina Foundation, Mattering: the credential is the unit: 75% by 2040
Microsoft Elevate, Mattering: 20 million credentials in two years
Walmart.org, Mattering: skills-first systems, signaled by worker data
Walmart.org, Belonging: portable records: “data mobility between systems”
